summary: Steel Shasta-Trinity NF lookout in Trinity County, CA; 1935 cab moved to Hayfork fairgrounds; NHLR-registered 2015. Build dates conflict.

facts.design: steel lookout tower; original 1935 cab since removed

staffing.status: 2011 visit form marks Staffed? No, while a comment in the same entry says staffed seven days a week, eight hours a day in fire season; current staffing unknown

access.note: Access road requires a sturdy vehicle with at least 6 inches of clearance; sign at pavement's end about 6 miles below the tower. No source says whether the tower itself is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: Road needs a sturdy vehicle with at least 6 inches of clearance. No source says whether the tower is open to visitors.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the cab a 1935 date. The 1951 USGS station description says the earlier lookout was destroyed in the early 1930s and a new one built about 600 feet southwest. The two dates do not reconcile, and the sources do not say which structure each refers to. The story reports both.
The register gives 6,992 ft (2,131 m), which matches the brief. A 1946 newspaper quote gives 6,895 feet for the station. The register figure is used.
The Forest Lookouts page heads the Reid telephone and 21-fire item with a 1940 date, but the same item cites the August 8, 1912 Trinity Journal. The item is dated 1912.

The 2011 visit form marks Staffed? No, but a comment in the same visit entry says the tower is staffed seven days a week, eight hours a day, during fire season. Both are reported in the story; current staffing is unknown.

notes_for_editor: Register and Forest Lookouts page carry the main facts. The Forest Lookouts page is a compiled set of newspaper clippings and survey notes, not a primary record. Current status (2026) is unverified: the newest visit report is 2011, and no current staffing, open-to-visitors or rental source was found. Access level left unset because no source says whether the tower is public. The firelookout.org California list shows Weaver Bally as a standing tower under NHLR US 1060, CA 105. An earlier FFLOS number, US 1790, CA 36, sits on that list's Warm Springs Mountain row (Los Angeles County), not this lookout, so it was removed at fact-check. A WebSearch returned AllTrails and Peakbagging pages, which describe the road as needing a high-clearance 4WD vehicle and give elevations of 6,990 and 6,971 ft; these were not read and are not cited.
